correctness.rationale: Two separately implemented exhaustive face enumerations both give 10012 augmented simplices. Explicit toggle partial matching gives 5002 augmented matched pairs, eight positive-dimensional critical simplices (six 4, two 5), and when empty pair removed one critical 0 vertex; complete oriented Hasse graph has 47968 edges and a topological order visiting all 10012 nodes. Signed integral gradient reductions give exactly zero 2-by-6 Morse differential. The Morse CW model has only 0,4,5-cells; Hurewicz \(\pi_4\cong H_4\) for the four-skeleton gives null attaching maps of both five-cells and the claimed \(\bigvee^6 S^4\vee\bigvee^2 S^5\). Modular ranks independently agree. Finite exhaustive program is an exact certificate of one finite statement, not a proof of unseen grids.

evidence: Outerplanar-graph theorem requires an outerplanar underlying graph. The \(4\times4\) grid contains three internally disjoint paths between two graph vertices and is not outerplanar.
Path-product theorem concerns categorical \(P_m\times P_n\), whereas the graph in this claim is the Cartesian \(P_4\mathbin{\square}P_4\), and the paper distinguishes the operations.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither theorem dominates the stated instance; the published planar wedge statement is a conjecture, not a proved implication. General arbitrary-graph matching-complex topology does not imply numerical sphere multiplicities here.

value.rationale: The balanced \(4\times4\) grid is the next canonical Cartesian-grid matching-complex case outside the 1-, 2-, and 3-row families prominent in the inspected literature. The nontrivial exact mixed-dimensional sphere wedge gives a strong reproducible benchmark and a natural nonouterplanar planar case supporting (without settling) the planar wedge conjecture. This goes beyond a routine numerical homology calculation through an explicit acyclic matching and integral attaching-map proof. It does not infer any uniform formula or paper-sized contribution.
